It looked like they were rolling right over us.''"<br />"''That's how.''"<br />"''Whoa!|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Erel Kersos]] and Dr. [[Kornell Divini]] upon seeing the [[Resolution (Venator-class)|''Resolution'']]|<ref name="MedStar">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Venator''-class Star Destroyer''',<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> also known as the '''''Venator''-class Destroyer''',<ref name="TCG: Revenge of the Sith">{{TCG|set=Revenge of the Sith|cardname=Venator-Class Destroyer}}</ref> '''Republic attack cruiser''',<ref name="DB:RAC">{{DB|starship|republicattackcruiser|Republic attack cruiser}}</ref> '''Jedi cruiser''',<ref name=":0" /> and later '''Imperial attack cruiser''',<ref name="Hasbro Imperial ''Venator'' model bio">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Titanium Series|pack=Imperial Attack Cruiser|altlink=http://hasbro.com/default.cfm?page=ps_results&product_id=18519}}</ref> was a [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] used extensively by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the later parts of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], as well as by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Characteristics==
===Dimensions===
[[File:Venator_Class_Star_Destroyer_CS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Left to right: Hangar areas, main [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]] [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]], [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and an auxiliary reactor.]]
A stock ship was 1,137 meters long, making it one of the largest capital ships capable of atmospheric operations, landing on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] to load and unload [[Troop/Legends|troops]] and vehicles.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

The ''Venator''-class was born from the success of the [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class assault ship]] and was designed by [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira Blissex]] for the purpose of serving as a medium-sized, versatile multi-role [[Warship/Legends|warship]].<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

===Roles===
While designed primarily for ship-to-ship combat,<ref name="DB:RAC" /> the ''Venator'' had secondary roles ranging from [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Carrier/Legends|carrier]], to military [[Transport/Legends|transport]] and [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] escort. The expanded carrier role made the ''Venator''-class popular amongst [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi starfighter|starfighter]] aces.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

As a popular multi-role warship of the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], the ''Venator'' was considered heavily armed and armored enough to lead assaults on Rim worlds like [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] as well as fast enough to chase down [[blockade runner]]s.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />
Due to being relatively less self-sufficient than other ships in the fleet, the ''Venator''-class often relied upon supply lines to aid long-range campaigns.<ref name="SOTG07" />

===Offensive and defensive systems===
<div style="float: right">[[File:VenatorTurbolasers-HH.png|thumb|200px|A ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer firing all batteries.]]</div>
The armament of a single ''Venator''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] consisted of eight dual [[DBY-827 heavy turbolaser turret/Legends|DBY-827 heavy turbolaser turrets]], two medium dual [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] cannons, fifty-two point-defense dual [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]],<ref name="RotS" /> and four [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] tubes.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

The ''Venator''-class's eight heavy dual turbolaser turrets were its main weapons and had two tracking modes. In its precise, long-range tracking mode, the DBY-827 could hit a target vessel at a range of ten light minutes. During close-range fights, the turrets could rotate in three seconds with their fast-tracking mode.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> In terms of firepower, these weapons rivaled the main battery on the later [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers]].

The DBY-827 had seven different power settings. This allowed the ''Venator''{{'s}} [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] to select a range of destruction, from a small strike to a vaporizing blow. As a true warship, the ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer could divert almost all of its reactor output to its heavy turbolasers when needed. As a result of this, a flotilla of ''Venator''s could break through the shields of a [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|battleship]] with ease.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

At the suggestion of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a heavy [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery|SPHA]] turbolaser cannon was installed within the ventral [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] bay of some ''Venator''-class ships of the [[Open Circle Fleet/Legends|Open Circle Fleet]]. These weapons were meant to protect the Star Destroyers while they opened their long ventral doors to the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army]] complement bays.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> They would be used to considerable effect during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].<ref name="RotS" />

===Propulsion systems===
[[File:BlockadeofFelucia.png|thumb|left|220px|The engine units of a Venator.]]
''Venator''s were equipped with powerful engines, a Class 1 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] with an effective range of 60,000 [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]]. Its main reactor could annihilate up to 40,000 tons of [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]] fuel per second, producing at maximum 3.6 × 10<sup>24</sup> watts of power.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> This power was routed to four primary thrusters, two secondary thrusters and four tertiary thrusters, with five on either side of the hyperdrive mounting.

The main engine room had several vertical power cylinders littering the room, with walkways on different levels providing access to onboard personnel.<ref name="COD">{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}}</ref>

===Complement===
Despite possessing powerful weaponry and being on par with the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class]], the ''Venator''-class was designed with an additional starfighter carrier role in mind. Its [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]] were far larger than those on other Star Destroyers like the ''Victory''-class.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

Prior to the formation of the Galactic Empire, a typical Republic Venator carried a complement of 420 fighters: 192 [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing]] or [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent starfighters]], 192 [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptors]], and at least 36 [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighters]]. The ship also typically maintained a variety of [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]] in its hangars. Since it was capable of entering a planet's atmosphere and landing on its surface, the pre-Imperial ''Venator''-class had a standard complement of 40 [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] and 24 military [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] for planetary operations.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

<div style="float: right">[[File:Venator_hangar.jpg|thumb|220px|The main hangar of a ''Venator''-class vessel.]]</div>
In addition to a standard ventral hangar bay, the bow of a Venator could open up to reveal a half kilometer long dorsal flight deck. This flight deck enabled the ''Venator''-class to rapidly launch hundreds of fighters. However, the slow opening and closing of the armored bow doors could leave the ship extremely vulnerable.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

Although strong shielding was used to compensate for this weakness, this design aspect would be entirely omitted from later Star Destroyer designs, such as the ''Imperator/Imperial''-class. On ships in the [[Open Circle Fleet/Legends|Open Circle Fleet]], a [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery|SPHA]] turbolaser cannon was positioned near the ventral hangar opening for the purpose of protecting the ship along the ventral arc. The ''Venator''-class also had hangar-openings on its port and starboard side. These were used to dock with [[Space station/Legends|space stations]], mooring towers, and larger [[Starship/Legends|starships]], for the purpose of transferring troops and materials.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />

===Command tower===
[[File:Venator_bridge.png|thumb|left|220px|The bridge of an Imperial ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer.]]
Because of its carrier role, the ''Venator''-class featured a novel dual bridge tower design. The port tower was the starfighter command bridge, while the starboard tower served as a standard helm and command bridge. On future designs, this dual bridge design was also employed.<ref name="RotS:ICS" />
A similar dual-tower design was also seen on the [[Secutor-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Secutor''-class Star Destroyer]],<ref name="EGTW" /> and the [[Maelstrom-class battle cruiser/Legends|''Maelstrom''-class battlecruiser]].<ref name="LbE">''[[Lead by Example]]''</ref>

The command bridge was designed with dual crew pits where operators would be stationed to control the ship's various functions. Officers would patrol walkways above and have a panoramic view to the outside.<ref name="RotS" /> This bridge design would become a standard feature on most Imperial warships.<ref name="SOTG01">''[[Starships of the Galaxy]]''</ref>

On top of each tower was a [[Hyperwave/Legends|hyperwave]] communications and scanner module. Its function was similar to the scanner globes on the ''Imperial''-class and other KDY vessels, but it had a flat shape.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> Flagships in ''Venator'' flotillas had red-painted conning towers to separate them from others.<ref name="TCWEP:DM">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode004.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Destroy ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

==History==
===Republic origin===
{{Quote|That's a Star Destroyer. ''Venator''-class.|[[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]]|<ref name="MedStar" />}}
[[File:Venator-WW.png|thumb|300px|A ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer present for the [[Battle of Mon Cala/Legends|Battle of Mon Cala]]]]
The ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer was designed and constructed by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]].<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> Such vessels were built in various shipyards such as the [[Allanteen VI shipyards/Legends|Allanteen Six shipyards]].<ref name="TCW:WS">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> The ''Venator''-class shared some design-characteristics with a [[Mandalorian warship (Venator-style)|warship]] class that served in the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusader]] fleet during the [[Mandalorian Wars]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] thousands of years before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="KOTOR17">[[Knights of the Old Republic 17|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 17]]</ref> In [[738 BBY]], during the [[Mandalorian Excision]], Republic forces used ships with a similar design.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> By the time of the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]], a predecessor to the later Venator-class was already in use with the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Outland Regions Security Force]], which [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]]'s brother served on. It was destroyed when [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark's]] [[Navcomputer virus|Navicomputer Virus]] caused it to emerge from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] in the middle of a star.<ref name="Agent of the Empire – Iron Eclipse 1">[[Agent of the Empire – Iron Eclipse 1|''Agent of the Empire – Iron Eclipse'' 1]]</ref>

''Venator''-class Star Destroyers were deployed in many battles during the Clone Wars, most notably during the Battle of Coruscant when upwards of a thousand such ships helped protect the capital,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections2">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> and played pivotal roles in the repulsion of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]] forces and the rescue of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="RotS" /> During the war, they were also commonly referred to as Jedi cruisers due to their widespread use as flagships by the [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi generals]] of the Republic.<ref name=":0">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Separatist forces categorized this kind of vessel as Cruiser-class, to contrast the Escort-class designation for smaller vessels, like the [[Arquitens-class light cruiser/Legends|''Arquitens''-class]] and [[Consular-class cruiser (Charger c70 retrofit)/Legends|''Consular''-class]].<ref name="GI">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref>

These warships were fast enough to pursue [[blockade runner]]s, while also being large enough to lead independent operations, such as the [[Siege of Cato Neimoidia|Battle of Cato Neimoidia]], [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]], and the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|Battle of Utapau]]. They could be used to land troops on [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] surfaces, and serve as escorts for larger battleships, but their primary role was as mainline cruisers and starfighter carriers.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /><ref name="DOTD">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>

As ships of the line, they were often grouped in lines of three to four ships.<ref name="TCWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Imperial period and beyond===
By the end of the Clone Wars, it had become the most popular capital ship of the Republic, although shortly after the formation of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], it was eclipsed by designs inspired by the [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class]].<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> Despite this, ''Venator''s were used to great effect in the early years of the Empire.<ref name="TFTS">{{DoD|The First to Strike}}</ref> In the Empire, these ships were stripped of the colorful markings of the Republic models.<ref name="Hasbro Imperial ''Venator'' model bio" /> At least two ''Venator''s were involved in pursuing the L-4000 smuggler ship ''[[Uhumele]]'' alongside a contingent of fighter squadrons.<ref name="EGTW" />

[[File:Imperialattackcruisers.png|thumb|left|250px|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].]]
Eventually, more robust vessels such as the ''Imperator''- and [[Tector-class Star Destroyer|''Tector''-class]] became favored, and the ''Venator'' and its variants were phased out.<ref name="RotS:ICS" /> This was partially due to its over-reliance on starfighters, as it went against the prevailing [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]] and due to its prominent position in the Republic Navy, which the Empire attempted to distance itself from.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

This led to even more fringe groups obtaining ''Venator''s, as well as several Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], who used them in their private defense fleets,<ref name="TFUCG" /> and for their various militias.<ref name="JKT">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/23039847571/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-7|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 7}}</ref> The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Supreme Strategist]] commanded a ''Venator'' Star Destroyer during the early years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. It was destroyed during an [[Mission to Mandalore (Zann Consortium)|engagement]] above [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] with a [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] fleet.<ref name="FoC" />

The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] used several ''Venator''s as flight schools for military pilots, alongside several ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and captured [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleships]]. The [[Vensenor/Legends|''Vensenor'']] was a notable vessel that served in this role.<ref name="EGTW" /> Imperial ''Venator''s were also used as part of the security cordon for the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]] to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]] during the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]].<ref name="FFGBOTF">{{FFGTCG|set=Balance of the Force|cardname=Along the Sanctuary Pipeline}}</ref>

At least one ''Venator'' served in Admiral [[Natasi Daala|Daala's]] [[Maw Irregular Fleet]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]]<ref name="Revelation" /> to [[44 ABY]].<ref name="ASC">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref> At least two were used in the [[Evacuation of Dac]] in [[137 ABY]], with one transformed into a drone ship and fitted with an ion pulse to distract the Sith-Imperial fleet.<ref name="Legacy-47" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Venpro.jpg|thumb|230px|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer profile shots.]]
The engine room of the ''Venator''-class is modeled after the Gravity Control System of the [https://macross.fandom.com/wiki/SDF-1_Macross SDF-1 Macross] from the first [[Wikipedia:The Super Dimension Fortress Macross|Macross]] anime series.<ref name="TCWEG:COD">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode009.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Cloak of Darkness}}</ref>

In ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]'', the ''Venator''-class is described both as serving the part of a destroyer escorting larger Republic battleships, and described as a battleship itself (the latter in the section on the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]). This is most likely a reference to different classification systems being in use, one of which labels Star Destroyers like the ''Victory''- and ''Venator''-classes being medium-sized destroyers, while another labels them as battleships.

In the same book, the [[Utapaun]]s are said to use "downscaled" warships, such as the [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser]]. This explains why the ''Dreadnaught''-class is often referenced as a cruiser rather than a [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] (even when many were rebuilt into [[Assault frigate/Legends|assault frigates]]), despite being smaller than both the Empire's Star Destroyers and their Star Cruisers. A similar system would be described by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] scholars as the Imperial Classification System in many of the [[West End Games]] sourcebooks.

In the early development of ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', the ''Venator''-class was seen in at least one or two promotional screenshots. It was then featured in the demo but was cut from the final game, though it can be modded back into the game completely. The unit was eventually included in ''Empire at War''{{'s}} expansion pack [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption|''Forces of Corruption'']] and can be purchased in the game's Skirmish free-play mode; it is not available, however, in story-related scenarios.
